title: Brickset's Weekly Chart: Sagrada Família Tops the Most-Viewed Sets
summary: Brickset's weekly page-view chart shows the Sagrada Família leading the pack, with a surprise return for a huge Chima set and big jumps for the Millennium Falcon and Minas Tirith.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brickset has published its regular "What's hot this week" chart, ranking sets by how many times their detail pages were viewed on the site. The Sagrada Família (21065) took the top spot with 7,517 views, just ahead of the enormous BIGBOX 'The ultimate battle for CHIMA' set (4407), which climbed into second place.

Elsewhere in the top ten, the UCS Millennium Falcon (75192) and The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith (11377) both jumped significantly compared with last week, landing at third and fourth respectively. Titanic (10294), The X-Files (21369), a Shrek-themed set (72423), the Star Trek Enterprise Bridge (11385), Tower Bridge (10214) and Donkey Kong Arcade (72051) rounded out the list.

Brickset notes that overall traffic was up too, with 1,725,907 set detail pages viewed across the site this week — over 52,000 more than the previous week.

## Why it matters
This kind of chart is a handy snapshot of what's capturing the community's attention right now, from architecture and licensed builds to big display pieces. For UK fans following display builds, Modular-style architecture sets and large-scale models, it's a useful pulse-check on what's trending before you commit shelf space or budget to your next build.

## What to watch next
It'll be worth keeping an eye on whether the Chima BIGBOX set's rise reflects renewed interest in retro/rare large sets, and whether the Minas Tirith and Millennium Falcon jumps are tied to any wider news or restocks — nothing on that is confirmed yet, so treat any reasons behind the movement as speculation for now.

title: LEGO NINJAGO Duskfall trailer lands – how do the sets compare?

bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO NINJAGO's Duskfall storyline has its first full trailer, following an early look at San Diego Comic-Con 2026. The three tie-in sets are already available (or landing 1 August in the US), with the full Duskfall release due in September.

Comparing the trailer to the builds:

- **71870 The Twin Titan Mechs** – The two mechs, piloted by Kai and Nya (and possibly Mira), closely match their animated look. Kai's mech keeps its golden arm guards, while Nya's carries her staff, and one mech features a jetpack, just like on screen.
- **71871 Battle at the Dragon's Blade** – The scene that inspired this set, a dragon perched on a giant sword emerging from a skull's mouth, doesn't appear in the new trailer, though it was briefly shown in an earlier teaser. How this moment fits into the story isn't yet clear.
- **71872 Ultra Dragon's Battle** – This set has the biggest differences from the trailer. The Great Devourer shown in the animation is notably larger than its LEGO model counterpart.

## Why it matters
Set-to-screen comparisons are a fun way for NINJAGO fans to see how faithfully models translate animated moments into brick form, and they can hint at future sets based on scenes not yet covered. For UK collectors and builders, it's also a heads-up on new NINJAGO stock arriving on shelves this year.

## What to watch next
With one Duskfall scene (the Dragon's Blade moment) still unaccounted for in the new trailer, there may be more sets or story reveals to come before the September launch. Watch for additional trailers or set announcements as Duskfall approaches.

It joins a run of LEGO sets based on Spielberg's back catalogue, including Indiana Jones, Back to the Future, Jurassic Park and the recent 21370 E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial, and has been compared to 76956 T. rex Breakout as a potential companion piece for a Spielberg-themed display shelf.

According to the review, this is the first time a Donkey Kong-branded box has been used, as earlier Donkey Kong sets carried Super Mario branding instead. The design team reportedly spent years developing the set and deliberately used 'The Elder Bricks' — LEGO elements from 1949 to 1977 — to match the game's vintage theme.

Retro arcade builds have become a popular niche for LEGO, appealing to both gamers and builders who enjoy playable models. A Donkey Kong-specific set with genuine interactive elements and vintage-style parts is a notable addition for Super Mario theme collectors and anyone building a home LEGO arcade display.

title: LEGO Guardian Dragon vs Pokémon Rayquaza: how the two display dragons compare
summary: A side-by-side look at LEGO's NINJAGO Guardian Dragon and the upcoming Pokémon Rayquaza set reveals two very different takes on the green display dragon, ahead of Rayquaza's 1 August release.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan builder Bricks by Mind has put two of LEGO's green dragon display models side by side: 71847 The Guardian Dragon from NINJAGO, and 72168 Rayquaza, the upcoming Pokémon set. Both feature a large green dragon paired with a single minifigure, but the similarities largely end there.

The Guardian Dragon is the bigger build, with 1,650 pieces and a £139.99 / $149.99 / €149.99 price tag, thanks in part to its two sprawling wings and a detailed natural base with rocks and flowing rivers. Rayquaza comes in smaller at 1,083 pieces and £119.99 / $129.99 / €129.99, perched on a more compact, man-made Sky Pillar base without large wings.

While The Guardian Dragon's base looks more detailed, it leaves little room for its included Wu minifigure. Rayquaza's simpler Sky Pillar base gives its Zinnia minifigure more space to stand and be posed, and Zinnia edges ahead on printing detail with wrap-around leg prints and fabric elements.

71847 The Guardian Dragon is available now, and 72168 Rayquaza is set to launch on 1 August 2026.

## Why it matters
If you're building a display shelf of large-scale LEGO dragons, this comparison is a handy guide to piece count, price and posability before deciding whether to pick up one or both. It also shows how different licensed and in-house LEGO themes tackle the same brief — a tall dragon plus one minifigure — in quite different ways.

Merriam revealed that controlling the barrels' speed was the toughest challenge, saying he 'rolled thousands of barrels down those tracks' during development. The team also tried various ways of returning barrels to the top, including gears and levers, before settling on a simpler solution — just using more barrels. The finished chute holds 14 barrels with room for up to 20, creating what Merriam calls an 'infinite barrel loop'.

## Why it matters
Designer insight like this gives builders a rare look at how LEGO translates classic gaming mechanics into physical, playable models.
